the_real_finding: This is not an EP009 problem and more attempts will not fix it. All four EP007 Shorts needed a local append-silence repair because their Algieba guides also failed the 0.02 tail gate, at 0.0361, 0.0594, 0.0295 and 0.0516. EP007's Short 01 failed twice at 0.0357 and 0.0361, a second call changing nothing. The route simply does not leave trailing digital silence in its output, so the gate fails it as a matter of course. EP009's 01 and 04 passing natively at 0.0002 and 0.0116 is the exception, not the norm.

established_remedy.name: append-silence repair on a derived copy
established_remedy.operation: append 12000 all-zero frames, 0.5 s at 24 kHz, to a derived copy; the source is never overwritten and the derived file records the source PCM sha256 as its prefix, so it is provably the source plus zeros
established_remedy.effect: tail energy becomes 0.0 and the mechanical gate passes
established_remedy.limitation: It repairs the gate. It does not recreate a missing phoneme. In EP007 the owner selected the source take by listening first, and that ordering is the point: the ear settles whether the ending is complete, then the pad satisfies the machine.
established_remedy.precondition: owner listening on the source take, then explicit authorization. Not applied here.

attempt_1.asr_note: one real substitution beyond orthography: 'inn' read as 'end'

attempt_3.asr_note: orthographic differences only; lexically the cleaner read

the_two_03_candidates.trade: Attempt 1 has the lower tail energy; attempt 3 has the cleaner word read and a noticeably faster read at 43.0 s against 51.0 s. Both are above every EP007 source that was successfully repaired, and attempt 3's 0.1626 is well above. Which of the two is usable is a listening call, and it is possible neither is.

corrected_hypothesis: An earlier reading in this session guessed the failures tracked the final phoneme, with the two passing scripts ending in a /t/ stop. EP007 refutes it: 'engagement' also ends in /t/ and still needed the pad. The route not padding its own output explains the data without the phoneme theory.

options_for_the_owner.note: EP007's own recommendation when an ending is clipped rather than merely unpadded. Worth considering for 03 specifically, whose two takes are the worst-tailed of all seven calls.

Eight of ten Algieba guides across two episodes have failed it and every one was resolved by padding rather than regeneration. The threshold lives in calibrate.py as a method-level choice and changing it is out of scope here; it would need its own decision.

limitations: Local ASR cannot prove an unclipped final phoneme and does not replace owner listening. Nothing here speaks to voice match, performance or register, which are judgments on Original C audio that does not yet exist.
